subject: Private deployment: PII, logging, and egress — follow-up & action items
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@serenhealth.com>
Cc: Siren Health Security <security@serenhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Private deployment call — PII, logging, egress

Thanks for the call this morning, Alex / Jamie — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we hand this to the engineering review: 

Summary (from our discovery):
- Scope: Ship inference calls to a customer-managed VPC (private deployment) to avoid sharing raw PHI/PII with hosted services.
- Data types: Tokenized PHI fields (patient name, MRN), free-text notes, and hashed identifiers for analytics.
- Primary constraints: 1) No long-term retention of raw transcript text beyond 24 hours, 2) Audit logs for every inference request retained for 90 days, 3) Egress to third-party services must be blocked except to approved S3 endpoints, 4) On-prem air-gapped environment capability is required for one pilot site.

Action items I captured:
1) Redwood to provide a network boundary sketch + suggested security group rules (Neha) — due by EOD Mon 5/17.
2) Siren to confirm which downstream services need access to embeddings/outputs (S3, data lake, internal analytics) — Alex/Jamie to confirm by 5/18.
3) Agree retention windows and exact fields considered PII — we had provisional 24h raw retention, hashed aggregations unlimited. Siren to confirm by 5/18.
4) Feasibility check on air-gapped on-prem deployment and install constraints — Redwood to list components that require outbound access.

Attachments I'm adding to this thread as a starting point: rdrw-network-sketch-v2.png (draft network boundary), rdrw-pii-mapping.csv (example mapping we use for other healthcare pilots).

Next meeting suggestion: Technical design review with Siren security & infra (30–45m) — propose Tue 5/19 10:00–10:45 PT. Please flag if that doesn't work.

Thanks — Monica

Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment call — PII, logging, egress

Monica — adding technical notes against the action items. Attaching a slightly updated sketch (same filename) and a short checklist for SG/NACL rules.

Notes: 
- Network boundary: We recommend two subnets in customer VPC: inference-subnet (private) and admin-subnet (restricted bastion). All outbound from inference-subnet must go through a VPC endpoint (Interface endpoint to our management plane if needed) or a NAT with strict SG rules. No public internet egress from inference-subnet by default.
- Egress exceptions: Allow only to the following destinations (examples): approved S3 bucket ARNs for result drops, the customer's monitoring endpoints (if necessary) over TLS, and our provisioning endpoint (only during deployment windows).
- Logging: We will emit per-request audit logs locally to a secure S3 bucket in the customer's account via VPC endpoint. Logs include timestamp, model version, token counts, request metadata (no raw-response unless explicitly requested). Retention policy is configurable — we can default to 90 days and support export to long-term archive under the customer's lifecycle.
- PII handling: We support automatic redaction hooks but do not modify customer data by default. For PHI, we recommend an ingestion preprocessor in-customer that strips or tokens sensitive fields before inference. If Siren requires zero-touch (no retention of raw text), we'll configure transient memory only and route logs to hashed-only artifacts.
- On-prem/air-gapped: The runtime requires the following outbound during initial install: package signing validation (one-time), license activation to a local license server (optional offline activation available), and metric bundle upload (optional; can be disabled). After install, component can be configured to operate fully without internet but with degraded remote support.

Open questions for the technical review: 
- Will Siren provide an S3 bucket in the same region for logs & outputs or prefer us to provision one in your account?
- For the air-gapped site, do you have an air-gap ambassador host we can use for package transfer?

I'll be ready to walk through the sketch on Tue 5/19.

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@serenhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Siren Health Security <security@serenhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment call — PII, logging, egress

Thanks, Monica & Neha — that's very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the tech review: 

1) Retention: The clinical team is firm on 0–24 hours for raw transcripts. Derived embeddings and hashed identifiers can be stored indefinitely for feature retrieval, but they must be stored in our region (us-east-1) and in our managed S3.
2) Auditing: We need immutable per-request audit logs (append-only) retained for 12 months for compliance. Can you confirm the logs include request_id, time, model_version, and a redaction flag? We need tamper-evidence (SSE + object lock) on the bucket.
3) Egress: No egress to 3rd-party analytics services. Only outbound approved: your provisioning endpoint (if strictly needed), and our internal S3. Any telemetry or error reports must be opt-in and only allowed over an admin channel.
4) On-prem pilot: We do have an air-gap ambassador host. We'll share access details once we sign the NDA addendum. For the pilot, the security team will need a runbook of manual install steps and checks.

Can you confirm whether the install-time outbound checks Neha mentioned can be met via a manual offline signing process? Also please confirm a contact at Redwood who will own the install runbook.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Turner | Head of Infrastructure
Siren Health
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment call — PII, logging, egress

Alex — great questions. Short answers and confirmed owners below so your security team can proceed with the NDA addendum and pilot planning: 

- Retention & storage: Confirmed — raw transcripts: 0–24h (default), derived embeddings & hashed identifiers: customer-controlled and stored in your S3 (us-east-1). Owner: Monica (contract + product config).
- Audit logs: We'll emit per-request logs with request_id, timestamp, model_version, token counts (no raw output). Redaction flag will be present if preprocessing removed sensitive fields. We support SSE-KMS and S3 Object Lock for tamper-evidence. Owner: Neha (implementation + runbook).
- Egress: Blocked by default. Allowed endpoints limited to your approved S3 buckets and the initial provisioning endpoint. Telemetry disabled unless explicitly enabled by your admin account. Owner: Dev Patel (deployment policy + security groups).
- Offline install path: We support an offline signing / package transfer workflow. We'll provide a signed bundle and a manual install runbook. Owner: Neha + Dev.

Next steps (owners + deadlines):
- 5/21: Neha to upload final network sketch and SG checklist to the shared Drive folder.
- 5/21: Monica to circulate NDA addendum template for the air-gap pilot.
- 5/22: Alex to confirm destination S3 bucket ARNs and share access pattern requirements.
- 5/25: Joint technical review (45m) — propose 10:00–10:45 PT.

I'll attach the egress checklist we referenced (sg-egress-checklist.pdf) and keep the drive folder updated. If anything is missing from this summary flag it here and I'll update.

Thanks — Monica
